== widgets.toml
# Herd widgets: one worker per ready task in the tracker docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.
# Written by `loopherd init`; yours to edit, loopherd never rewrites it.
repo = "<root>/widgets"
args = ["--permission-mode", "auto"]

[queue]
template = "issue"
# Fill in from docs/agents/issue-tracker.md: a shell command printing
# "<number> <type> <skill> <slug>" per ready task, oldest first. Then adapt
# the issue template's done check and prompt to the same tracker. Until this
# is set, `loopherd herds` reports the herd invalid and feed refuses it.
source = ""
# Fill in the same way: a shell command printing "<key> <title>" per open task
# that isn't ready, leaving out blocked ones and keeping ones waiting on the
# human; `loopherd status` counts its lines. Or drop it.
backlog = "(fill in)"
max = 3

[template.issue]
params = ["number", "type", "skill", "slug"]
name = "{herd}-{number}"
branch = "{type}/{number}-{slug}"
# Fill in from docs/agents/issue-tracker.md:
# done, a shell command that exits 0 once task {number} is closed, its braces
# doubled. Until it's set no member counts as done, so feed never retires one.
merged = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr list --repo acme/widgets --head {branch} --state merged --json number --jq 'length > 0' | grep -qx true"
prompt = '''
You're {name}, working task {number} on branch {branch} in {worktree}.

Fill in from docs/agents/issue-tracker.md: each line marked (fill in), with this
tracker's own commands.

Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)` as in the commands below.

1. Read task {number} and every comment on it. (fill in)
2. Claim it: comment `claimed by {name}` on it. (fill in)
3. Build it with the {skill} skill.
4. Before calling it done, run each check and fix what fails:
   - `cargo test`
   - `cargo fmt --check`
5. Push the branch as acme:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push -u origin HEAD`.
   Then open a pull request into main with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr create --repo acme/widgets --base main --head {branch} --assignee acme --title "<title>" --body "<summary>"`.
   Link it on task {number}, so the task closes when the PR merges. (fill in)
6. Finish with `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.

If main moves under you, merge origin/main into your branch; never
rebase or force-push.

If you hit a question only the human can answer, stop rather than guess: mark
task {number} needs-info (fill in), comment the question and the options you
see on it, then `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.
'''

[lead]
prompt_file = "widgets-lead.md"
# From [lead_defaults] when init ran. Off means the lead asks the human.
merge = false
install = false
rebase = false
new_cards = false
design_escalation = false
blocked_dialogs = false
follow_ups_ready = false
merge_guard = "hook"
== widgets-lead.md
You're {name}, the lead of herd {herd}, in {worktree}, a detached checkout of
widgets you never commit in. No human is in this pane.

Read `loopherd --skill` in full, its Lead section most closely. Tasks come from the tracker docs/agents/issue-tracker.md describes. Fill in from docs/agents/issue-tracker.md: how a worker's task closes when its PR merges. (fill in)
Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)`. You run the shepherd's loop for {herd}'s workers: feed, watch, verify
each worker's PR with a reviewer subagent, send only blocking findings back
to the member, and the after-merge steps.

Your switches (off means the human does it; ask with a question report):
{switches}

Your review-round limit: {review_rounds}.

Grilling is always the human's.

Start now:
1. `loopherd status` and `loopherd reports --all`, to see where the herd is.
2. `loopherd feed {herd} --dry-run`, then `loopherd feed {herd}` if it reads right.
3. Arm `loopherd watch {herd} --timeout 3600` as a background task, and
   re-arm after every exit but `{herd} drained`: on that, report done and
   stop. On `<member> merged`, run `loopherd feed {herd}`,
   which retires it once its issue is closed. On `<name> claimable`, feed.
   Exit 2 is your heartbeat: check each worker's PR for a merge and run
   `loopherd feed {herd} --dry-run`.

When you need the human, run `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact
question>"` and end your turn. With merge off, a merge question carries the PR
link, any PR that must merge first, and the line
`! GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr merge <n> --repo acme/widgets --merge --match-head-commit <full sha>`
for the head your reviewer verified. Single-quote that question ('...', not
"..."): double quotes run the $(...) and leak the token.
== AGENTS.md
# Agent instructions

## loopherd

A loopherd herd works this repo's ready issues, one worker per issue on its
own branch. A worker reads `docs/agents/loopherd.md` for how to claim, build,
check, hand in and report an issue, and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for
the tracker.
== docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
# Issue tracker

Issues live in Linear.
== docs/agents/triage-labels.md
# Triage Labels

The skills speak in five canonical triage roles. This file maps each role to
the label string this repo's issue tracker uses.

| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `needs-triage` | `needs-triage` | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue |
| `needs-info` | `needs-info` | Waiting on reporter for more information |
| `ready-for-agent` | `ready-for-agent` | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent |
| `ready-for-human` | `ready-for-human` | Requires human implementation |
| `wontfix` | `wontfix` | Will not be actioned |

When a skill mentions a role, use the corresponding label string from this
table. Edit the "Label in our tracker" column to match the labels you use.
== docs/agents/loopherd.md
# Working a task in a loopherd herd

loopherd starts one worker per ready task, each in its own worktree on its
own branch. The worker's prompt names the task, the branch and the exact
commands; this doc says what each step is for. How the tracker works is in
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

Fill in from docs/agents/issue-tracker.md: each section marked (fill in).

## Claiming

Read the task and every comment first. Then comment `claimed by <member>`
on it, with your member name. A task someone else has claimed isn't yours.
(fill in)

## Branch names

`<type>/<number>-<slug>`: the herd file's queue source gives each task its
type, number and slug. loopherd creates the branch and its worktree; work
only there. If main moves under you, merge `origin/main` into your
branch; never rebase or force-push.

## Checks

Before calling the work done, run each check and fix what fails:

- `cargo test`
- `cargo fmt --check`

## Handing in

Push the branch and open a PR with `--base main`. Hand the work in on the task, so it closes when the work merges;
loopherd counts the task done once it is closed. (fill in)

## Stopping on a question

When only the human can answer, stop rather than guess: mark the task
`needs-info`, comment the question and the options you see on it, then
report it. (fill in)

## Reporting

Tell the shepherd how the work ended:

- Done: `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.
- Stopped on a question: `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.
